audit_findings.title: IDR claim may be absent from both OE and the denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $182 million FY2025 IDR allocation, equal to 38.1% of the $478.2 million anchor; $145 million for the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring IDR distributions reduce OE attributable to common and Class D units; IDRs are not represented in the 190.185221 million-unit denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: As discussed below, the IDRs represent the right to receive increasing percentages, up to a maximum of 50%, of the cash we distribute from operating surplus (as defined below) in excess of $0.503125 per unit per quarter.
audit_findings.explanation: The IDR claim is demonstrated by the filings, but its omission from OE is unresolved because no anchor reconciliation was supplied. Its filed scale is large enough to change the per-unit valuation materially if the $478.2 million anchor retained any cash belonging to the IDR holder.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor line by line to GAAP cash flow and explicitly identify IDR deductions. If absent, rerun every scenario after deducting a normalized IDR cash stream before division by units.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual preferred claim is not fully reflected
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.5 billion liquidation claim; $118.125 million computed annual distribution at 7.875%; the claim equals 17.2% of $8.740 billion base equity value and $7.89 per diluted unit
audit_findings.mechanism: The preferred units rank ahead of common and Class D units and must enter through either normalized preferred distributions deducted from OE or a preferred claim deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In September 2025, the Partnership closed a private offering of 1.5 million of its 7.875% Series A Fixed-Rate Reset Cumulative Redeemable Perpetual Preferred Units (the “Series A Preferred Units”) at an offering price of $1,000 per unit.
audit_findings.explanation: The senior perpetual claim and its absence from the disclosed bridge are demonstrated. Whether the anchor deducts the partial FY2025 allocation is unresolved, but a partial-period charge cannot represent the continuing $118.125 million annual burden. The claim is large enough to materially change value per unit and the buy threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to the $34 million preferred allocation, normalize the full-year distribution using the reset provisions, and rerun the valuation using either the normalized OE deduction or the $1.5 billion bridge deduction, never both.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method investments may be double counted
audit_findings.magnitude: $196 million of FY2025 operating-cash-flow distributions, equal to 41.0% of the $478.2 million anchor, alongside $1.610 billion of stakes added to the bridge, equal to 18.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate earnings or distributions can enter OE while the same ownership interests are separately capitalized through stakes_net in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash provided by operating activities for 2025 also includes $196 million cash distributions received from unconsolidated affiliates that are deemed to be paid from cumulative earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The affiliate cash distributions and bridge addition are demonstrated, but double counting is an unresolved possibility because the OE reconciliation is missing. Either filed amount is large enough to affect the valuation conclusion if the cash flow and stake value overlap.
audit_findings.action: Trace equity-method earnings, distributions from cumulative earnings, excess distributions, contributions and affiliate maintenance capital through OE by investee. Rerun after purging all stake-derived cash flows from OE or removing the corresponding stake value from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Full acquisition claims are paired with only two months of Parkland results
audit_findings.magnitude: 51.517198 million Class D units, equal to 27.1% of the 190.185221 million-unit denominator; Parkland contributed only November and December results, including $195 million of net income
audit_findings.mechanism: The full Class D denominator applies immediately, while the OE anchor contains only two months of acquired operations and partial-period interest, preferred, tax, maintenance-capital and IDR burdens.
audit_findings.evidence: Parkland's revenue and net income, excluding intercompany transactions, since the acquisition date to December 31, 2025 included in our consolidated statement of operations were $ 3.17 billion and $ 195 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated and material by denominator scale. Its value direction is mixed: omitted Parkland operating cash flow understates value, while omitted continuing financing and senior-claim costs overstate it. The as-filed anchor convention avoids crediting an unobserved run rate but does not make the numerator and claims economically coherent.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-year Parkland normalization covering operating earnings, cash taxes, maintenance capital, interest, preferred distributions and incremental IDRs, retain the full common-plus-Class-D denominator, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: TanQuid creates a post-year-end perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $239 million consideration, $346 million assumed debt and $45 million acquired cash; $194 million net acquisition cash outflow, equal to 2.2% of base equity value; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 cash and debt context reflects TanQuid, but the FY2025 OE anchor excludes its operating cash flow and acquisition-related interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction was funded using cash on hand and amounts available under the Partnership's Credit Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the record does not isolate TanQuid earnings, maintenance capital or interest. Omitted operations could understate value while omitted interest could overstate it. The transaction's disclosed net cash scale is modest relative to base equity value, but that comparison does not establish the recurring OE effect.
audit_findings.action: Extract acquisition-date-to-June TanQuid operating earnings, cash taxes, maintenance capital and interest from the June 2026 records, annualize only supported recurring items, and rerun with all TanQuid assets and financing either included or excluded consistently.

audit_findings.title: Accrued environmental obligations may remain an unfunded senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $224 million environmental liabilities plus $208 million asset-retirement obligations at June 30, 2026, totaling $432 million; 4.9% of base equity value and $2.27 per diluted unit
audit_findings.mechanism: Remediation and retirement settlements reduce future OE if captured as maintenance spending; otherwise the unfunded accrued claims require an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, it has recorded estimated undiscounted liabilities for these sites totaling $168 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The liabilities are demonstrated, but omission from OE is unresolved. Even the conservative assumption that the entire $432 million is incremental and immediately deducted would reduce base value from $45.95 to approximately $43.68 per unit and bull value from $51.98 to approximately $49.71, both still far below the $75.60 market price. It therefore does not change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile projected remediation and tank-removal payments to maintenance capital and OE to prevent omission or double counting; deduct only the portion not already captured.
